facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: CNX Resources Corp has a clear financial base for the current period: audited FY2025 statements, three unaudited 2026 quarters and a nine-month income and cash flow statement are all supplied, and the debt, facility, cash-paid and commitment notes allow facility-level work. On the management measure of trailing adjusted EBITDAX, gross and net leverage both sit below two times at September 30, 2026, cash interest is covered about eight times, and the funding position is almost entirely revolver capacity rather than cash. The maturity wall is empty until the revolvers and the CNXM notes fall due in 2029 and 2030. Three conditions qualify the view. First, the earnings measure is management's non-GAAP adjusted EBITDAX, which removes unrealized derivative gains while leaving realized settlements in; it is not the credit agreement's consolidated EBITDA, which is not supplied. Second, the parent and CNXM groups carry separate debt, covenants and guarantors, so consolidated ratios blur which group bears which claim. Third, figures from the thousand-dollar filings and the million-dollar supplements are combined only where stated, and the trailing cash-interest figures mix a full-year amount net of capitalized interest with interim amounts that carry no such label.

Trailing figures 1,322 (March 2026), 1,280 (June 2026) and 1,276 (September 2026) are as printed (Q1 supplement page:14; Q2 supplement page:13; Q3 supplement page:13). Check: 292 + 400 + 290 + 294 = 1,276. 2. Net debt: December 31, 2025: 2,421.359 less 0.779 = 2,420.580; March 31, 2026: 2,366.853 less 3.748 = 2,363.105; June 30, 2026: 2,223.745 less 6.162 = 2,217.583; September 30, 2026: 2,278.924 less 1.977 = 2,276.947 (US$m). Management net debt also deducts restricted cash and prints 2,275 at September 30, 2026 (supplement page:12); 2,278.924 less 1.977 less 2.429 = 2,274.518, which rounds to 2,275 and is consistent. 3. Total debt / adjusted EBITDAX: 2,421.359 / 1,247 = 1.94; 2,366.853 / 1,322 = 1.79; 2,223.745 / 1,280 = 1.74; 2,278.924 / 1,276 = 1.79. Net: 2,420.580 / 1,247 = 1.94; 2,363.105 / 1,322 = 1.79; 2,217.583 / 1,280 = 1.73; 2,276.947 / 1,276 = 1.78. Sensitivity on principal: 2,299.850 / 1,276 = 1.80. 4. Trailing cash interest (US$m): FY2025 154.598 (10-K page:155); March 2026 = 154.598 less 53.325 plus 63.384 = 164.657; June 2026 = 154.598 less 74.290 plus 79.365 = 159.673; September 2026 = 154.598 less 135.812 plus 139.234 = 158.020. Undrawn facilities: December 2025: 1,172.003 + 567.250 = 1,739.253; March 2026: 1,295.703 + 495.000 = 1,790.703; June 2026: 1,216.353 + 510.000 = 1,726.353; September 2026: 1,140.053 + 533.000 = 1,673.053. Check on the parent revolver at September 30, 2026: 1,400.000 less 232.850 less 27.097 = 1,140.053. 7. Principal by maturity: 2029: 232.850 + 67.000 = 299.850; total 299.850 + 400 + 500 + 600 + 500 = 2,299.850. Carrying: 2,299.850 less discounts 4.533, 3.235 and 2.067 = 2,290.015; less issuance costs 11.091 = 2,278.924. 8. Leases: finance 5.753 + 27.492 = 33.245 and operating 45.420 + 71.321 = 116.741 at September 30, 2026; December 31, 2025 finance 5.095 + 24.991 = 30.086 (agrees with the 10-K lease table) and operating 48.453 + 104.955 = 153.408. 9. Operating cash flow less capital expenditures: FY2025 1,028.957 less 494.988 = 533.969; nine months 2025 731.908 less 320.574 = 411.334; nine months 2026 810.558 less 451.058 = 359.500. 10. Cross-check of the earnings measure: nine months 2026 net income 716.329 + interest expense 119.081 + income tax 168.204 + DD&A 405.490 = 1,409.104; adding the supplement's exploration expense of 9 (4 + 3 + 2) gives 1,418.104, against EBITDAX before adjustments of 608 + 415 + 395 = 1,418 in the supplements. Agreement is within rounding.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: CNX Resources Corp is a publicly listed, non-sponsored producer whose business is selling Appalachian natural gas, mostly from Shale and a smaller Coalbed Methane position, through short-term market-priced contracts to a few large marketers, cushioned by a hedge book and supported by owned gathering systems. For a creditor the operating model is stable in volume but exposed to price, basis and counterparty concentration, and its reported revenue includes derivative gains that are largely non-cash. The 2026 transactions are mainly liability management and shareholder returns: new 2034 notes against the repurchase of the 2029 notes, a convertible that matured into shares rather than cash, and buybacks that exceeded free cash generation in the nine months. The pack shows no sponsor, no dividend recapitalisation and no documented priming, uptier or drop-down; that absence is limited to seven filings and is not a clearance, because indentures, credit agreements and the proxy statement are not supplied. The midstream subsidiary sits in a separate credit group with its own notes and revolver, a structural feature rather than an observed behaviour.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: No acquisition, sponsor transaction or merger was announced in the pack for the cutoff window. The new debt and related capital actions of the nine months ended September 30, 2026 are as follows. CNX issued 500,000 aggregate principal amount of 5.875% Senior Notes due March 2034 at par under an indenture dated February 26, 2026 with UMB Bank, N.A. as trustee, guaranteed by the restricted subsidiaries that guarantee the CNX Credit Facility; interest is payable on March 1 and September 1 beginning September 1, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:22). In the same period CNX repurchased all 500,000 of its 6.00% Senior Notes due January 2029, recording a 12,009 loss on debt extinguishment (page:22), and the supplement places that loss in Q1 2026 (Q1 supplement page:12). The 2.25% Convertible Senior Notes matured on May 1, 2026; the remaining 208,553 principal was settled through the issuance of 12,636,743 net shares and no cash was exchanged, and the related capped calls expired with 3,605,684 shares delivered to CNX and retired (page:23). The use of proceeds of the 2034 notes is Insufficient Information: the filings state both events but do not link them, so the link is an analyst reading only. The liquidity effect is visible in the balance sheet: the 2026 convertible notes and the January 2029 notes are gone, leaving the May 2029 revolvers as the nearest maturity (accepted financial handoff). The revolver borrowing base and elected commitments were unchanged at 2,400,000 and 1,400,000 on May 13, 2026 (page:19). Earlier, in the nine months ended September 30, 2025, CNX issued 200,000 of additional 7.25% Senior Notes due March 2032 at 100.5% of par (page:23) and on January 27, 2025 acquired Apex Energy II, LLC's upstream and associated midstream business for cash consideration of about 517,599 (page:17). Other 2026 capital actions: share repurchases of 432,781 in the nine months at an average price of 35.08 per share (page:35), and a July 1, 2026 sale of federal tax credits for about 30,000 net of costs, which approximated carrying value (page:18). Subsequent to September 30, 2026 and inside the pack: share count and hedge positions as of October 2026, and updated 2026 guidance in the Q3 supplement (adjusted EBITDAX 1,290 to 1,310 and capital expenditures 571 to 586, US$m, page:7). Draft or pending transactions: none in the pack.

facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: 1. Cash buybacks less internally generated cash: purchases of common stock 434,678 less (operating cash flow 810,558 less capital expenditures 451,058 = 359,500) = 75,178 (US$000), nine months 2026. Sources: Q3 10-Q page:10, page:11; the same 359,500 appears in the accepted financial handoff. 2. Net revolver borrowings, nine months 2026: CNX revolver 1,549,700 less 1,516,850 = 32,850; CNXM revolver 273,050 less 238,800 = 34,250; total 67,100. Cross-check: revolver balances 200,000 plus 32,750 = 232,750 at December 31, 2025 and 232,850 plus 67,000 = 299,850 at September 30, 2026, a rise of 67,100 (Q3 10-Q page:11, page:21). 3. Segment shares are not calculated; the text compares the printed segment revenue lines only. 4. Realized price against NYMEX: 2.58 against 2.95 per the supplement table; the 0.37 gap is not asserted as a differential because other components (basis 0.85, BTU conversion 0.11, derivative cash settlement 0.37) are printed separately (Q3 supplement page:7).

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: CNX Resources Corp has a moderate credit risk profile on the evidence supplied: low leverage and no maturities before 2029 are offset by single-basin gas price exposure and shareholder returns that ran ahead of free cash flow. The strongest support is debt of USD 2,278.924 million against trailing adjusted EBITDAX of USD 1,276 million (1.79x), cash interest cover of 8.07x, USD 1,673.053 million of undrawn facilities and 461.2 Bcf hedged for 2026. The weakest point is that the earnings measure is management's non-GAAP figure, covenant headroom is unverified and nine-month buybacks of USD 434.678 million exceeded operating cash flow less capital expenditures of USD 359.500 million. Gas prices after the hedges thin in 2028 and 2029, and the pace of buybacks, decide the outcome. [Assessment: Analyst Interpretation, confidence Medium.]

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The first finding is leverage and coverage. At September 30, 2026 CNX Resources Corp carried USD 2,278.924 million of balance-sheet debt and USD 1.977 million of cash, which is 1.79x gross and 1.78x net of trailing adjusted EBITDAX of USD 1,276 million, against 1.94x at FY2025; trailing cash interest cover is 8.07x. These are management-measure results, not covenant ratios, and a principal-based gross figure is 1.80x (Documentary Fact from the financial handoff; the ratios are calculated there). The mechanic is that adjusted EBITDAX removes unrealized derivative gains but keeps realized settlements, so it tracks cash earnings better than reported revenue, which includes a derivative gain of USD 160.563 million in Q3 2026; the implication is low leverage tolerance risk today, with a cushion that depends on gas prices.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The second finding is liquidity and refinancing. Cash is minimal, so liquidity is revolver capacity: USD 1,140.053 million is unused on the parent revolver (after USD 27.097 million of letters of credit) and USD 533.000 million on the CNXM revolver, which the parent does not guarantee. Undrawn capacity fell from USD 1,790.703 million at March 31, 2026 to USD 1,673.053 million. Both revolvers mature on May 17, 2029, together with USD 299.85 million drawn, so the refinancing risk is concentrated in one year; the notes follow in 2030 (USD 400 million, CNXM), 2031 (USD 500 million), 2032 (USD 600 million) and 2034 (USD 500 million), and nothing falls due in 2026 to 2028 (Documentary Fact).

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The third finding is capital allocation. In the nine months of 2026 CNX repurchased shares for USD 432.781 million, while cash purchases of USD 434.678 million exceeded operating cash flow less capital expenditures of USD 359.500 million by USD 75.178 million, with net revolver borrowings of USD 67.100 million (Analyst Interpretation of cited figures). The convertible notes were settled in shares without cash and the 5.875% notes due 2034 were issued in the same period in which the 6.00% notes due 2029 were repurchased. The mechanic is that discretionary buybacks consume the cash flow that services the revolvers; the program is discretionary and can be reduced, which limits the credit risk if management responds in a price downturn. The use of proceeds of the 2034 notes is not stated (Insufficient Information).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Low leverage on management's measure and strong interest cover give debt service a wide margin today [Documentary Fact]. There are no maturities before 2029 and the notes are staggered across 2030 to 2034 [Documentary Fact]. A large hedge book, with 461.2 Bcf covered for 2026 and 409.4 Bcf for 2027, supports cash flow visibility for roughly two years [Documentary Fact]. Revolver capacity of USD 1,673.053 million gives liquidity without cash on hand [Documentary Fact]. The business is large and long-lived, with 9.7 Tcfe of proved reserves, 72.2% proved developed, and owned gathering systems that reduce reliance on third parties [Documentary Fact]. Buybacks and the absence of dividends are discretionary, so management can redirect cash to creditors in stress [Analyst Interpretation].

The binding limitations are that no executed financing document, rating or market input is supplied and that the text extraction is chunked and flattened, so table structure and any charts are not independently verified. No source is blocked, no identity boundary is unresolved and no conflict between sources was found. This is source sufficiency only; downstream analytical handoffs are not a readiness condition.

### Reader summary

| On management's adjusted EBITDAX, gross leverage is 1.79x and cash interest cover 8.07x, with undrawn facilities of 1,673.053 and no debt due before 2029. The picture rests on a non-GAAP earnings measure. | Medium | Adjusted EBITDAX is a management measure; covenant EBITDA and headroom are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Debt was 2,278.924 at September 30, 2026, against adjusted EBITDAX of 1,276 over the last twelve months, giving 1.79x gross and 1.78x net. | Low leverage on this basis; the result depends on how the earnings measure treats derivative gains. | Medium |
| Cash interest cover was 8.07x over the last twelve months. | Ample cover on the measure used, with cash interest drawn from two filings that differ slightly in wording. | Medium |

| Cash is minimal; liquidity is undrawn revolver capacity, 1,673.053 in total, of which 533.000 belongs to the midstream group. | Parent liquidity is the parent revolver only; midstream capacity is not freely available to the parent. | Medium |
| No debt matures until 2029; the revolvers and 2030 to 2034 notes make up the schedule. | Refinancing risk is back-ended, but both revolvers fall due together in 2029. | High |

| Non-debt claims sit outside the debt figure: purchase obligations of 1,248,484 (US$000), surety bonds, leases and letters of credit. | They add fixed claims on cash flow that debt-only leverage omits. | Medium |
### Financial base view

CNX Resources Corp has a clear financial base for the current period: audited FY2025 statements, three unaudited 2026 quarters and a nine-month income and cash flow statement are all supplied, and the debt, facility, cash-paid and commitment notes allow facility-level work. On the management measure of trailing adjusted EBITDAX, gross and net leverage both sit below two times at September 30, 2026, cash interest is covered about eight times, and the funding position is almost entirely revolver capacity rather than cash. The maturity wall is empty until the revolvers and the CNXM notes fall due in 2029 and 2030. Three conditions qualify the view. First, the earnings measure is management's non-GAAP adjusted EBITDAX, which removes unrealized derivative gains while leaving realized settlements in; it is not the credit agreement's consolidated EBITDA, which is not supplied. Second, the parent and CNXM groups carry separate debt, covenants and guarantors, so consolidated ratios blur which group bears which claim. Third, figures from the thousand-dollar filings and the million-dollar supplements are combined only where stated, and the trailing cash-interest figures mix a full-year amount net of capitalized interest with interim amounts that carry no such label.

### Reader summary

In 2026 it refinanced notes, settled its convertible in shares and bought back stock. | Medium | No sponsor, ownership detail, indentures or use-of-proceeds statement is supplied, so governance and legal capacity cannot be tested. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Three marketers each exceeded 10% of FY2025 customer revenue. | Counterparty concentration adds collection and renewal risk, though sales are short term. | High |

| The 5.875% senior notes due March 2034 were issued, the 6.00% notes due January 2029 repurchased and the convertible notes settled in shares in 2026. | The maturity wall moved out and no cash was paid at the convertible's maturity; the notes' use of proceeds is not stated. | Medium |

### Business and transaction view

CNX Resources Corp is a publicly listed, non-sponsored producer whose business is selling Appalachian natural gas, mostly from Shale and a smaller Coalbed Methane position, through short-term market-priced contracts to a few large marketers, cushioned by a hedge book and supported by owned gathering systems. For a creditor the operating model is stable in volume but exposed to price, basis and counterparty concentration, and its reported revenue includes derivative gains that are largely non-cash. The 2026 transactions are mainly liability management and shareholder returns: new 2034 notes against the repurchase of the 2029 notes, a convertible that matured into shares rather than cash, and buybacks that exceeded free cash generation in the nine months. The pack shows no sponsor, no dividend recapitalisation and no documented priming, uptier or drop-down; that absence is limited to seven filings and is not a clearance, because indentures, credit agreements and the proxy statement are not supplied. The midstream subsidiary sits in a separate credit group with its own notes and revolver, a structural feature rather than an observed behaviour.

| Segment mix | Q3 2026 natural gas, NGLs and oil revenue: Shale 341,589, Coalbed Methane 30,685, Other 242 | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:32 | Shale carries nearly all sales; Coalbed Methane contributed a pre-tax loss of 1,731 in the quarter (page:33), so it adds volume but not profit |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

No acquisition, sponsor transaction or merger was announced in the pack for the cutoff window. The new debt and related capital actions of the nine months ended September 30, 2026 are as follows. CNX issued 500,000 aggregate principal amount of 5.875% Senior Notes due March 2034 at par under an indenture dated February 26, 2026 with UMB Bank, N.A. as trustee, guaranteed by the restricted subsidiaries that guarantee the CNX Credit Facility; interest is payable on March 1 and September 1 beginning September 1, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:22). In the same period CNX repurchased all 500,000 of its 6.00% Senior Notes due January 2029, recording a 12,009 loss on debt extinguishment (page:22), and the supplement places that loss in Q1 2026 (Q1 supplement page:12). The 2.25% Convertible Senior Notes matured on May 1, 2026; the remaining 208,553 principal was settled through the issuance of 12,636,743 net shares and no cash was exchanged, and the related capped calls expired with 3,605,684 shares delivered to CNX and retired (page:23). The use of proceeds of the 2034 notes is Insufficient Information: the filings state both events but do not link them, so the link is an analyst reading only. The liquidity effect is visible in the balance sheet: the 2026 convertible notes and the January 2029 notes are gone, leaving the May 2029 revolvers as the nearest maturity (accepted financial handoff). The revolver borrowing base and elected commitments were unchanged at 2,400,000 and 1,400,000 on May 13, 2026 (page:19). Earlier, in the nine months ended September 30, 2025, CNX issued 200,000 of additional 7.25% Senior Notes due March 2032 at 100.5% of par (page:23) and on January 27, 2025 acquired Apex Energy II, LLC's upstream and associated midstream business for cash consideration of about 517,599 (page:17). Other 2026 capital actions: share repurchases of 432,781 in the nine months at an average price of 35.08 per share (page:35), and a July 1, 2026 sale of federal tax credits for about 30,000 net of costs, which approximated carrying value (page:18). Subsequent to September 30, 2026 and inside the pack: share count and hedge positions as of October 2026, and updated 2026 guidance in the Q3 supplement (adjusted EBITDAX 1,290 to 1,310 and capital expenditures 571 to 586, US$m, page:7). Draft or pending transactions: none in the pack.

Asset-sale proceeds of 48,723 also contributed |

| Convertible settled in shares | 208,553 principal settled by issuing 12,636,743 net shares; share exchange of 122,098 principal in December 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:23; 10-K page:145) | Documentary Fact | The equity-linked debt was retired by issuing shares rather than cash; the same period then saw cash repurchases of shares, so the dilution was partly offset |

| Structure | Parent credit group excludes CNXM, its subsidiaries and its general partner; CNX is not a guarantor of the CNXM notes or revolver (Q3 10-Q page:20, page:21) | Analyst Interpretation | Two creditor pools with separate guarantors. No documented transfer between them; legal capacity to move assets is Insufficient Information because the indentures are not supplied |

Feasibility: undrawn facilities of 1,673.053 (US$m) in the accepted financial handoff | Analyst Interpretation | Kept separate: capacity is untested, willingness is documented, feasibility is supported by revolver availability |

1. Cash buybacks less internally generated cash: purchases of common stock 434,678 less (operating cash flow 810,558 less capital expenditures 451,058 = 359,500) = 75,178 (US$000), nine months 2026. Sources: Q3 10-Q page:10, page:11; the same 359,500 appears in the accepted financial handoff.

It covers the consolidated group (CNX Resources Corporation and subsidiaries), with the parent and the CNX Midstream Partners LP (CNXM) credit groups kept apart, for FY2025 and the periods to Q3 2026. It works from the upstream readiness, financial and business handoffs only and reads no source text.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| CNX Resources Corp has a moderate-risk profile: gross leverage 1.79x, cash interest cover 8.07x, undrawn facilities of 1,673.053 and no debt due before 2029. Gas price exposure and buybacks above free cash flow are the weak points. | Medium | Earnings are a management non-GAAP measure and covenant headroom, indentures and ratings are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Debt of 2,278.924 against trailing adjusted EBITDAX of 1,276 gives low leverage on management's measure. | Leverage leaves room to absorb a price fall, but the measure excludes unrealized derivative gains by management's choice. | Medium |
| Liquidity is almost all revolver capacity, and both revolvers mature together in 2029. | A single 2029 refinancing event covers most of the liquidity and 299.85 of debt. | Medium |

| Nine-month cash buybacks of 434.678 exceeded operating cash flow less capital expenditures of 359.500. | Shareholder returns are partly revolver-funded, which would erode headroom if repeated. | Medium |
| Revenue is single-basin, market-priced and concentrated in a few marketers, with 461.2 Bcf hedged for 2026. | Cash flow is protected for about two years and then depends on prices. | Medium |
### Credit view

CNX Resources Corp has a moderate credit risk profile on the evidence supplied: low leverage and no maturities before 2029 are offset by single-basin gas price exposure and shareholder returns that ran ahead of free cash flow. The strongest support is debt of USD 2,278.924 million against trailing adjusted EBITDAX of USD 1,276 million (1.79x), cash interest cover of 8.07x, USD 1,673.053 million of undrawn facilities and 461.2 Bcf hedged for 2026. The weakest point is that the earnings measure is management's non-GAAP figure, covenant headroom is unverified and nine-month buybacks of USD 434.678 million exceeded operating cash flow less capital expenditures of USD 359.500 million. Gas prices after the hedges thin in 2028 and 2029, and the pace of buybacks, decide the outcome. [Assessment: Analyst Interpretation, confidence Medium.]
### Key findings

The first finding is leverage and coverage. At September 30, 2026 CNX Resources Corp carried USD 2,278.924 million of balance-sheet debt and USD 1.977 million of cash, which is 1.79x gross and 1.78x net of trailing adjusted EBITDAX of USD 1,276 million, against 1.94x at FY2025; trailing cash interest cover is 8.07x. These are management-measure results, not covenant ratios, and a principal-based gross figure is 1.80x (Documentary Fact from the financial handoff; the ratios are calculated there). The mechanic is that adjusted EBITDAX removes unrealized derivative gains but keeps realized settlements, so it tracks cash earnings better than reported revenue, which includes a derivative gain of USD 160.563 million in Q3 2026; the implication is low leverage tolerance risk today, with a cushion that depends on gas prices.

The second finding is liquidity and refinancing. Cash is minimal, so liquidity is revolver capacity: USD 1,140.053 million is unused on the parent revolver (after USD 27.097 million of letters of credit) and USD 533.000 million on the CNXM revolver, which the parent does not guarantee. Undrawn capacity fell from USD 1,790.703 million at March 31, 2026 to USD 1,673.053 million. Both revolvers mature on May 17, 2029, together with USD 299.85 million drawn, so the refinancing risk is concentrated in one year; the notes follow in 2030 (USD 400 million, CNXM), 2031 (USD 500 million), 2032 (USD 600 million) and 2034 (USD 500 million), and nothing falls due in 2026 to 2028 (Documentary Fact).

The third finding is capital allocation. In the nine months of 2026 CNX repurchased shares for USD 432.781 million, while cash purchases of USD 434.678 million exceeded operating cash flow less capital expenditures of USD 359.500 million by USD 75.178 million, with net revolver borrowings of USD 67.100 million (Analyst Interpretation of cited figures). The convertible notes were settled in shares without cash and the 5.875% notes due 2034 were issued in the same period in which the 6.00% notes due 2029 were repurchased. The mechanic is that discretionary buybacks consume the cash flow that services the revolvers; the program is discretionary and can be reduced, which limits the credit risk if management responds in a price downturn. The use of proceeds of the 2034 notes is not stated (Insufficient Information).

The fourth finding is the business risk. Production is 92% natural gas, sold at market prices under short-term contracts in one basin, mainly through Shale; three marketers each exceeded 10% of FY2025 customer revenue. Hedges cover 461.2 Bcf for 2026, 409.4 Bcf for 2027, 233.1 Bcf for 2028 and 38.2 Bcf for 2029, so revenue visibility is about two years. Fixed commitments sit outside the debt figure: unconditional purchase obligations of USD 1,248.484 million, surety bonds, leases and letters of credit (Documentary Fact). In a weak-price year these fixed costs compress margin against variable revenue.

The fifth finding is structure and information. The parent and CNXM are separate creditor pools: the parent does not guarantee the CNXM notes or revolver and parent covenants exclude CNXM, so consolidated ratios blur which group bears which claim. Covenant compliance is stated for both groups but no ratio or headroom is supplied, and the indentures, credit agreements, ratings and proxy statement are not in the pack, so legal capacity for distributions, liens and asset transfers is untested (Insufficient Information).
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Low leverage on management's measure and strong interest cover give debt service a wide margin today [Documentary Fact]. There are no maturities before 2029 and the notes are staggered across 2030 to 2034 [Documentary Fact]. A large hedge book, with 461.2 Bcf covered for 2026 and 409.4 Bcf for 2027, supports cash flow visibility for roughly two years [Documentary Fact]. Revolver capacity of USD 1,673.053 million gives liquidity without cash on hand [Documentary Fact]. The business is large and long-lived, with 9.7 Tcfe of proved reserves, 72.2% proved developed, and owned gathering systems that reduce reliance on third parties [Documentary Fact]. Buybacks and the absence of dividends are discretionary, so management can redirect cash to creditors in stress [Analyst Interpretation].

Weaknesses. Earnings rest on a management non-GAAP measure and the covenant definition is not supplied, so covenant headroom cannot be shown [Insufficient Information]. Revenue is single-basin, market-priced and short-term, so unhedged volumes and basis follow Appalachian prices, and hedges thin after 2027 [Documentary Fact]. Buybacks exceeded free cash generation in the nine months and revolver borrowings rose [Analyst Interpretation]. Liquidity depends on two revolvers that mature together in 2029, one of them at the CNXM level that the parent does not guarantee [Documentary Fact]. Fixed commitments of USD 1,248.484 million, surety bonds and leases add claims outside the debt figure [Documentary Fact]. Customer concentration in a few marketers is a counterparty risk [Documentary Fact]. Governance and legal capacity cannot be tested without the executed documents and the proxy statement [Insufficient Information].
### Credit assessment
| Item | Judgment | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Fundamental credit view | Moderate risk: low leverage and a clear maturity profile against price, concentration and distribution risks | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Financial base view and chart tables of the financial handoff; business and transaction view of the business handoff |

| Thesis | Low-leverage, hedged Appalachian gas producer whose credit quality depends on gas prices after the hedges thin and on discipline in shareholder returns | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Leverage, liquidity and maturity tables; buyback funding and hedge rows |
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Gas price and basis after hedges roll off | Single-basin, market-priced, short-term sales; hedges fall from 461.2 Bcf for 2026 to 38.2 Bcf for 2029 | Revenue and cash flow fall in a price downturn while fixed commitments remain; leverage rises quickly from a low base | Material |

| Shareholder returns above free cash flow | Cash buybacks of USD 434.678 million exceeded operating cash flow less capital expenditures of USD 359.500 million, with net revolver borrowings of USD 67.100 million | Revolver usage rises and liquidity headroom narrows if repeated | Material |

| Revolver concentration in 2029 | Both revolvers mature on May 17, 2029; cash on hand is USD 1.977 million | One refinancing event covers most liquidity; the CNXM revolver is outside the parent group | Material |

| Reliance on a management earnings measure | Adjusted EBITDAX excludes unrealized derivative gains; covenant EBITDA not supplied | Leverage and cover may differ from covenant ratios; headroom is unknown | Material |

| Off-balance-sheet fixed commitments | Purchase obligations of USD 1,248.484 million, surety bonds of USD 285.482 million, leases and letters of credit | Fixed claims on cash flow beyond the debt figure | Minor |
| Customer concentration | Three marketers each exceeded 10% of FY2025 customer revenue | Counterparty or contract disruption affects a large part of revenue | Minor |
## Calculations

None new. Every figure is carried from the financial handoff (ratios, liquidity, maturities, buyback comparison) or the business handoff (hedge volumes, customer concentration, net revolver borrowings of 67,100 thousand and the excess of cash buybacks over operating cash flow less capital expenditures of 75,178 thousand, shown here in USD million). Amounts are USD; the underlying filings state thousands and the supplements state millions.

| Use of proceeds of the 5.875% notes due 2034 not stated | The link to the repurchase of the 6.00% notes is an inference | Capital allocation | Minor | Check the offering document |
| Parent and CNXM stand-alone financials not supplied | Group-level leverage cannot be separated | Structure | Material | Obtain stand-alone or guarantor information |
